key_insight: The paper shows that large reasoning models can reveal an inherent “latent safety awareness” when their original queries and own reasoning traces are replayed, enabling safer responses without heavy manual labeling.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical alignment strategy for deploying reasoning models more safely by using model-generated signals to trigger safety analysis only when needed, preserving normal behavior for benign queries.
method: SFT adds an explicit safe tag to unsafe-query examples so the model learns to continue with safety analysis and guidance after its initial reasoning.
DPO is then used to improve the correctness and stability of the generated safety analysis and guidance.
All training responses are generated by the model itself, and the trigger is designed to be adaptive rather than always-on.
evidence_signal: On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, the method reduced average attack success rate by 24.65% on harmful benchmarks and 36.72% on jailbreak benchmarks, with little impact on general performance.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on model-generated supervision and triggered safety behavior, robustness may depend on the quality of the model’s own initial reasoning and the reliability of the safe-trigger detection policy.
paper_title: Adaptive and Explicit safe: Triggering Latent Safety Awareness in Large Reasoning Models
